report.source_text: In accordance with infectious disease consult, our patient underwent methyl prednisolone pulse therapy (1 g/d) for 3 days, and then prednisolone (1 mg/kg/d) as a maintenance therapy was initiated. Later, the patient was confused with right hemiparesis. Therefore, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) (25 g/d for 5 days) was initiated for the patient, which resulted in the improvement of both mental state and clinical symptoms.

report.source_text: After 3 months of clinical follow-up, the patient was still blind (no light perception) without pupillary light reflex. Muscle forces returned to normal; nevertheless, a wide-based gait was still observed (which was not reliable due to blindness). MRI also showed no new lesions. Prednisolone was tapered (10 mg/d) and patient received warfarin (international normalized ratio 2.2).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old man with recent PCR-confirmed COVID-19 infection developed abrupt complete right eye vision loss and left eye visual impairment with moderate headache. Initial neurological exam was notable for no light perception in right eye and partial vision in left eye. Brain MRI on admission showed bilateral acute infarctions in parietal and occipital lobes. CSF analysis was negative for neurotropic viruses including SARS-CoV-2, and autoimmune encephalitis panel and inflammatory markers were negative. Clinical progression included complete vision loss in left eye and MRI showed lesion extension involving cerebellum, frontoparietal lobes, corpus callosum, and pons. The patient was treated with methyl prednisolone pulse therapy followed by maintenance and IVIg after neurologic deterioration, which improved mental status and symptoms. At 3 months follow-up, vision loss persisted without pupillary reflex, MRI showed no new lesions, muscle strength normalized, and gait was wide-based. Treatment included prednisolone taper and warfarin anticoagulation. These findings support diagnosis of post–COVID-19 encephalitis with ischemic lesions and immune-mediated CNS involvement.
